newsitem.title: GERMANY: German builders seek to protect real pay in 1997.
newsitem.headline: German builders seek to protect real pay in 1997.

text.p: German construction sector trade union IG Bau said on Tuesday that it would not be anouncing a specific 1997 pay demand but that it would seek to protect real wages for the 1.3 million workers in the sector from falling.
"We shall not be naming any figure in any form yet," said IG Bau chairman Klaus Wiesehuegel.

Wiesehuegel said in the text of a speech for delivery to a news briefing that the union saw other 1997 wage agreements such as those reached in the large metal and engineering sectors as "guiding indicators".

He added that the union would also be seeking a reinstatement of the so-called 13th-month end-of-year bonus and the maintenance of sick-pay entitlements at 100 percent of salary. It also wanted clear agreements on payment of compensation to workers during bad weather.
Wiesehuegel said it therefore made no sense to name an individual pay figure, as the union wanted the final deal to include all these elements.
Construction workers were awarded a 1.85 percent pay increase for 1996 last April.
